paper.title: Job Displacement, Unemployment, and Crime: Evidence from Danish Microdata and Reforms
paper.journal: Journal of the European Economic Association
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement and no Statistics Denmark project number is given. …

registers.name_in_paper: the police and courts (Central Police Register)
variables_mentioned: conviction outcome (incarceration, suspended sentence, fine, settlement, no charge/warning)
start and end dates of incarceration

registers.name_in_paper: Integrated Database for Labor Market Research (IDA, Den Integrerede Database for Arbejdsmarkedsforskning)
registers.role: treatment (mass layoffs, displacement), firm size, sample frame

registers.name_in_paper: Central Register of Labour Market Statistics (CRAM)
registers.role: treatment timing (weekly receipt of UI and social assistance benefits)
variables_mentioned: received benefits (UI and SA) for each worker in each week of the year

registers.role: outcomes and controls (labor income, nonlabor income, total income)

registers.name_in_paper: the Ministry of Education (completed and ongoing schooling)
variables_mentioned: education category: high school or less, vocational, university or greater

registers.role: sample frame (UI fund membership and eligibility)
variables_mentioned: membership in an unemployment insurance fund

linkages: all six data sources are linked by the Central Person Register (CPR) number
charged individuals are matched by the police station to their CPR number and followed from charge to court conviction through the police case number; co-offenders share a case number
workers are matched to firms and workplaces through IDA firm and workplace identifiers, which are consistent over time
family members are assigned a family identification number in the Population Register; a household is a set of individuals residing at the same address

sample.universe: Anyone residing in Denmark for more than 3 months (assigned a CPR number); the estimation samples are drawn from the Danish employer-employee registry over 1985-2001
sample.unit_of_observation: individual x year for the crime and income regressions; firm x year for the firm-size regression of Table 2
selection_rules: the firm experiences a mass-layoff event in y0 = 1990,...,1994: firm size in y0 at least 30% below the firm's peak employment between y0-5 and y0-1, for firms with 30 workers or more (first event used if several)
false closings -- where 30% or more of the workers in the closing firm transition to the same firm -- are excluded from the mass-layoff definition
workers need at least 3 years of tenure in y0-1, defined as continuous, full-time employment with the same employer
individuals aged 19-39 in y0-1 (aged 20-40 at the time of displacement)
individuals with two or more jobs between y0-3 and y0-1 are excluded
individuals enrolled in education between y0-3 and y0-1 are excluded
within the high-tenure sample, a worker is displaced if his firm has a mass layoff in y0 and he transitions from employment in y0-1 to unemployment in y0, measured as receipt of unemployment benefits
five separate samples are constructed, one for each mass-layoff year y0 = 1990,...,1994, and pooled; nondisplaced high-tenure workers can appear in the control group of all five samples
sample.period: displacement years y0 = 1990-1994; each worker is followed from 5 years before to 7 years after displacement over a 17-year balanced panel (1985-2001)
sample.n_observations: 5,167,318 individual-year observations in the baseline regressions (2,782,402 in the t = -5 to +1 window); 1,973,619 in the placebo regressions of Table 3; 326,157 firm-year observations in Table 2 (371,887 including closings)
sample.n_individuals: 154,694 high-tenure individuals over the five samples y0 = 1990-1994; 9,382 firms in Table 2

construction_notes: Crime_it = 1 if individual i commits an offense and is charged at time t and the crime led to a conviction in any year t' >= t; criminal events leading to no charges, warnings or other infrequent outcomes are eliminated
the timing used is that of the offense, not of the charge, conviction or prison term; on average the lag between offense and conviction is 172 days (150 days for displaced workers)
offenses occurring on a day prior to the first week of post-displacement unemployment are recoded as occurring at t = -1
crimes are grouped into three categories: property crimes, violent crimes and driving under the influence (DUI)
alternative mass-layoff definition: a 30% decline relative to a firm-specific linear trend n_j,y = alpha_j + beta_j * y fitted on 1980-1989 employment
the baseline mass-layoff reference point is the firm's peak employment in the five years prior to the layoff
pre-2007 municipality definitions are used throughout: 270 municipalities, giving 3,510 municipality x time fixed effects over the 13 years of event time

predicted UI benefits follow the statutory formula b_iy = min{90% x earnings_{i,y0(i)-1}, maximum_y}, with annual maxima of 127,608 DKK in 1990-1991, 132,600 DKK in 1992, 137,020 DKK in 1993 and 132,340 DKK in 1994-1996, apportioned by the number of months each law applies; the 90% replacement rate is unchanged over the period
potential (statutory) benefit periods, not realised time in unemployment, define the benefit-regime indicators of Table 6; their cohort-by-cohort lengths are displayed in Figure 4
workers are classified into three education categories: high school or less, vocational, university or greater

claims.statement: In the year of a mass layoff, firm employment falls by 67.808 employees relative to the year before the event (all firms, conditioning on firm survival).

treatment.label: Mass-layoff event at the firm (indicator for year Mass-Layoff Year relative to the event)

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research): firm identifiers and employment

definition.value: A firm experiences a mass layoff in year y0 = 1990,...,1994 if its size is 30% lower than its peak employment between y0-5 and y0-1, for firms with 30 workers or more; if a firm has several events the first is used. The regression enters one indicator per year before and after the event, with Year -1 as the reference.

timing.value: year relative to the mass-layoff event, from -5 to +5

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research): firm employment counts

definition.value: Number of employees of the firm in the given year; in column (2) firms that exit the data following a closing are kept and assigned a firm size of 0.

timing.value: firm-year, from 5 years before to 5 years after the mass-layoff event

units.value: employees

magnitude.interpretation: a 30% decline is an uncommon and statistically large event

estimand.target_population: firms with 30 workers or more experiencing a mass layoff in y0 = 1990-1994
estimand.time_horizon: the mass-layoff year (t = 0)

population.description: Danish private firms with 30 workers or more that experience a mass-layoff event -- firm size in y0 at least 30% below peak employment between y0-5 and y0-1 -- in y0 = 1990,...,1994; 9,382 firms
population.period: firm-years around mass-layoff events in y0 = 1990-1994
population.selection: Firms with fewer than 30 workers are excluded; column (1) conditions on firm survival after the mass layoff, column (2) includes firms that exit after a closing with firm size set to 0; false closings (30% or more of workers moving to the same firm) are excluded

identification.source_of_variation: timing of firm-level mass layoffs (30% decline from the firm's five-year peak employment) in y0 = 1990-1994

key_assumptions.assumption: Absent the mass-layoff event, firm size would have continued on the path captured by the year effects and the reference year -1; the pre-event indicator variables test this.
key_assumptions.supported_by: the pre-mass-layoff indicator variables are not significant at the 10% level

key_assumptions.assumption: A 30% decline relative to peak employment is an uncommon, statistically large event rather than ordinary firm-size variation.
key_assumptions.supported_by: post-mass-layoff indicators significant at the 1% level in both columns

key_assumptions.assumption: Firm exit is handled by assigning a firm size of 0 (column (2)); column (1) conditions on firm survival after the mass layoff.
key_assumptions.supported_by: the two columns are reported side by side

implies_edges.from: firm closing (exit from the data)
implies_edges.to: inclusion in the estimation sample

threats_discussed: firms may be on a downward trend so that the 30% change is anticipated
false closings, where 30% or more of the workers transition to the same firm
robustness_checks: mass layoffs defined relative to a firm-specific 1980-1989 employment trend
50-employee firm size threshold (Online Appendix Section B.1.1)

claims.statement: Among high-tenure workers in the five years before displacement, workers who will be displaced in 1990 are no more likely than workers who will not be displaced to commit a property offense leading to a conviction.

treatment.label: Future Displaced Worker

register_source.value: IDA (firm identifiers and mass-layoff definition) combined with CRAM (receipt of unemployment benefits in y0)

definition.value: Indicator equal to 1 for an individual observed in the period y0-5 to y0-1 who will be displaced in any year y0 between 1990 and 1994, inclusive; column (1) is the sample of the y0 = 1990 displacement year.

timing.value: status measured prospectively: crime is measured in the five years before the future displacement

register_source.value: the police and courts (Central Police Register): criminal charges matched to the individual's CPR number by the police station and followed from charge to court conviction; no DST register code is given in the paper

definition.value: Indicator equal to 1 if the individual commits a property offense at time t and is convicted in the same or any subsequent year; the timing used is that of the offense, not of the charge or conviction. Offenses occurring on a day prior to the first week of post-displacement unemployment are recoded as occurring at t = -1. Linear probability model, so 0.0057 = 0.57 percentage points.

timing.value: annually, in event time t = y - y0 relative to the displacement year, over the balanced panel t = -5 to +7

units.value: probability of committing an offense leading to a conviction (linear probability model; 0.0017 = 0.17 percentage points)

magnitude.interpretation: ranging between 0.00 and 0.17 ppt, are not statistically significant at the 10% level

estimand.time_horizon: the five years before displacement, y0-5 to y0-1

population.ages: 19-39 in the year before displacement; 20-40 at the time of displacement
population.period: the five years before displacement, y0-5 to y0-1, for y0 = 1990-1994
subgroups_defined: workers who will be displaced in some y0 between 1990 and 1994
workers who will not be displaced between 1990 and 1994
population.selection: Conditioned on surviving the five high-tenure screens in y0-1 (3+ years of continuous full-time tenure with the same employer, no two or more jobs between y0-3 and y0-1, not enrolled in education, private-sector firm) and on being male; displacement is conditioned on the employer experiencing a mass layoff and on the worker claiming unemployment benefits in y0

identification.source_of_variation: comparison, within the same employer, municipality and year, of the current convictions of high-tenure workers who will be displaced in some y0 between 1990 and 1994 with those of workers who will not

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on year, municipality and employer fixed effects and on age, tenure, annual wage, education, industry, firm size and marital status, future displacement status is unrelated to current crime unless workers are selected on an unobserved propensity to commit crime.
key_assumptions.supported_by: the placebo table itself; controls and three sets of fixed effects

unresolved_confounders: displaced workers may be unobservably more responsive to layoffs -- essential heterogeneity (footnote 12)

register_source.value: IDA (firm identifiers and mass-layoff definition) combined with CRAM (receipt of unemployment benefits in y0)

definition.value: Indicator equal to 1 for an individual observed in the period y0-5 to y0-1 who will be displaced in any year y0 between 1990 and 1994, inclusive; column (4) is the sample of the y0 = 1993 displacement year.

timing.value: status measured prospectively: crime is measured in the five years before the future displacement

register_source.value: the police and courts (Central Police Register): criminal charges matched to the individual's CPR number by the police station and followed from charge to court conviction; no DST register code is given in the paper

definition.value: Indicator equal to 1 if the individual commits a property offense at time t and is convicted in the same or any subsequent year; the timing used is that of the offense, not of the charge or conviction. Offenses occurring on a day prior to the first week of post-displacement unemployment are recoded as occurring at t = -1. Linear probability model, so 0.0057 = 0.57 percentage points.

timing.value: annually, in event time t = y - y0 relative to the displacement year, over the balanced panel t = -5 to +7

units.value: probability of committing an offense leading to a conviction (linear probability model; 0.0017 = 0.17 percentage points)

magnitude.interpretation: ranging between 0.00 and 0.17 ppt, are not statistically significant at the 10% level

population.ages: 19-39 in the year before displacement; 20-40 at the time of displacement
population.period: the five years before displacement, y0-5 to y0-1, for y0 = 1990-1994
subgroups_defined: workers who will be displaced in some y0 between 1990 and 1994
workers who will not be displaced between 1990 and 1994

claims.statement: The eight post-displacement coefficients are jointly different from one another: the impact of displacement on crime is not a constant, flat effect over the eight post-displacement years.

treatment.label: Job displacement during a mass layoff (post-displacement coefficients delta_+0 to delta_+7 jointly)

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research) for firm size, firm identifiers and employment; the Central Register of Labour Market Statistics (CRAM) for weekly receipt of unemployment benefits

definition.value: A high-tenure worker is displaced if (a) his firm experiences a mass-layoff event in year y0 -- firm size in y0 at least 30% below the firm's peak employment between y0-5 and y0-1, for firms with 30 workers or more -- and (b) he transitions from employment in y0-1 to unemployment in y0, measured as the receipt of unemployment benefits. Entered as indicator variables 1(k years after displacement) for k = -5,...,+7, with k = -1 the omitted reference year.

timing.value: years 0 to +7 after displacement

outcome.label: Any Crime (property or violent crime) -- the eight post-displacement coefficients of Table 4 taken jointly

register_source.value: the police and courts (Central Police Register): criminal charges matched to the individual's CPR number by the police station and followed from charge to court conviction; no DST register code is given in the paper

definition.value: Indicator equal to 1 if the individual commits an offense (property or violent) at time t and is convicted in the same or any subsequent year; the timing used is that of the offense, not of the charge or conviction. Offenses occurring on a day prior to the first week of post-displacement unemployment are recoded as occurring at t = -1. Linear probability model, so 0.0057 = 0.57 percentage points.

timing.value: annually, in event time t = y - y0 relative to the displacement year, over the balanced panel t = -5 to +7

units.value: F statistic (F(7, 9381) = 2.91) for the null hypothesis delta_0 = delta_1 = ... = delta_+7

magnitude.interpretation: both p-values are substantially below 0.01, implying that the null hypothesis is rejected at 1%

register_source.value: statutory benefit durations by displacement cohort (Figure 4), applied to displacement timing from IDA and benefit receipt recorded weekly in the Central Register of Labour Market Statistics (CRAM)

definition.value: Six indicator variables built from the statutory (potential) benefit periods of each displacement cohort -- one for each benefit period (passive, active, social assistance) and one for each transition between them -- rather than from the realised time spent in unemployment; the pre-displacement year is the omitted category. Lengths are set by Lov 434 of 1993, Lbk 16 of 1994 and Lbk 29 of 1996 and are displayed by cohort in Figure 4.

timing.value: the years in the potential social assistance period, after benefit eligibility expires

register_source.value: the police and courts (Central Police Register): criminal charges matched to the individual's CPR number by the police station and followed from charge to court conviction; no DST register code is given in the paper

definition.value: Indicator equal to 1 if the individual commits a property offense at time t and is convicted in the same or any subsequent year; the timing used is that of the offense, not of the charge or conviction. Offenses occurring on a day prior to the first week of post-displacement unemployment are recoded as occurring at t = -1. Linear probability model, so 0.0057 = 0.57 percentage points.

timing.value: annually, in event time t = y - y0 relative to the displacement year, over the balanced panel t = -5 to +7

units.value: probability of committing a property offense leading to a conviction, relative to the pre-displacement year (linear probability model; 0.0032 = 0.32 percentage points)

estimand.target_population: high-tenure Danish male workers displaced during a mass layoff in 1990-1994 who reach the benefit period or transition in question
estimand.time_horizon: the years in the potential social assistance period, after benefit eligibility expires

population.description: High-tenure Danish male private-sector workers -- at least 3 years of continuous full-time employment with the same employer in y0-1, aged 19-39 in y0-1 (20-40 at displacement), no second job and not enrolled in education between y0-3 and y0-1 -- pooled over the five displacement-year samples y0 = 1990,...,1994, both displaced and nondisplaced
population.ages: 19-39 in the year before displacement; 20-40 at the time of displacement
population.period: displacement years 1990-1994; each worker observed over the 17 years of the balanced panel, event time t = -5 to +7
population.selection: Conditioned on surviving the five high-tenure screens in y0-1 (3+ years of continuous full-time tenure with the same employer, no two or more jobs between y0-3 and y0-1, not enrolled in education, private-sector firm) and on being male; displacement is conditioned on the employer experiencing a mass layoff and on the worker claiming unemployment benefits in y0

identification.source_of_variation: the 1993 Act on an Active Labor Market (Lov 434 of June 30, 1993), the Executive Order Lbk 16 of January 11, 1994 (4 years of passive and 3 years of active benefits) and the amendment Lbk 29 of January 23, 1996 (passive period cut to 2 years), which hit the 1990-1994 displacement cohorts at different points of their post-displacement spell and so shift the statutory timing of benefit periods cohort by cohort

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on individual fixed effects, municipality-by-time fixed effects and age controls, displacement during a mass layoff is independent of the worker's unobserved propensity to commit crime -- there is no dynamic endogenous selection of workers into displacement.

definition.value: Six indicator variables built from the statutory (potential) benefit periods of each displacement cohort -- one for each benefit period (passive, active, social assistance) and one for each transition between them -- rather than from the realised time spent in unemployment; the pre-displacement year is the omitted category. timing.value: the year of the transition from passive to active benefits, for workers with less than 26 weeks of full-time employment in the last three years

definition.value: Indicator equal to 1 if the individual commits a property offense at time t and is convicted in the same or any subsequent year; the timing used is that of the offense, not of the charge or conviction. units.value: probability of committing a property offense leading to a conviction, relative to the pre-displacement year (linear probability model; 0.0032 = 0.32 percentage points)

population.description: High-tenure Danish male private-sector workers -- at least 3 years of continuous full-time employment with the same employer in y0-1, aged 19-39 in y0-1 (20-40 at displacement), no second job and not enrolled in education between y0-3 and y0-1 -- pooled over the five displacement-year samples y0 = 1990,...,1994, both displaced and nondisplaced
population.ages: 19-39 in the year before displacement; 20-40 at the time of displacement
population.period: displacement years 1990-1994; each worker observed over the 17 years of the balanced panel, event time t = -5 to +7

claims.statement: In the year of displacement nonlabor income -- all public transfers and residual income -- is multiplied by 2.4.

treatment.label: Job displacement during a mass layoff (year of displacement)

register_source.value: IDA (Integrated Database for Labor Market Research) for firm size, firm identifiers and employment; the Central Register of Labour Market Statistics (CRAM) for weekly receipt of unemployment benefits

definition.value: A high-tenure worker is displaced if (a) his firm experiences a mass-layoff event in year y0 -- firm size in y0 at least 30% below the firm's peak employment between y0-5 and y0-1, for firms with 30 workers or more -- and (b) he transitions from employment in y0-1 to unemployment in y0, measured as the receipt of unemployment benefits. Entered as indicator variables 1(k years after displacement) for k = -5,...,+7, with k = -1 the omitted reference year.

timing.value: the year of displacement (t = 0)

register_source.value: the Income Register (SKAT)

definition.value: Nonlabor income: all public transfers and the residual income; the reported figure is a multiplicative change.

timing.value: the year of displacement (t = 0)

units.value: multiplicative factor relative to pre-displacement nonlabor income

magnitude.interpretation: nonlabor income is multiplied by 2.4 in the year of displacement

estimand.target_population: high-tenure Danish male workers displaced during a mass layoff in 1990-1994
estimand.time_horizon: the year of displacement (t = 0)

population.description: High-tenure Danish male private-sector workers -- at least 3 years of continuous full-time employment with the same employer in y0-1, aged 19-39 in y0-1 (20-40 at displacement), no second job and not enrolled in education between y0-3 and y0-1 -- pooled over the five displacement-year samples y0 = 1990,...,1994, both displaced and nondisplaced
population.ages: 19-39 in the year before displacement; 20-40 at the time of displacement
population.period: displacement years 1990-1994; each worker observed over the 17 years of the balanced panel, event time t = -5 to +7
population.selection: Conditioned on surviving the five high-tenure screens in y0-1 (3+ years of continuous full-time tenure with the same employer, no two or more jobs between y0-3 and y0-1, not enrolled in education, private-sector firm) and on being male; displacement is conditioned on the employer experiencing a mass layoff and on the worker claiming unemployment benefits in y0

identification.source_of_variation: firm-level mass layoffs between 1990 and 1994 -- a 30% decline in firm employment relative to the firm's peak over the previous five years, for firms with 30 workers or more -- hitting high-tenure workers who are unlikely to separate otherwise; identification is within municipality and year

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on individual fixed effects, municipality-by-time fixed effects and age controls, displacement during a mass layoff is independent of the worker's unobserved propensity to commit crime -- there is no dynamic endogenous selection of workers into displacement.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 3 placebo: the current convictions of workers who will be displaced are not significantly different from those of workers who will not be displaced; the pre-displacement coefficients of Table 4 are jointly insignificant
